units.translation: In ⟦1⟧ there is of course deliberate exaggeration. The story was treated by Phrynichus in the ⟦2⟧; whether with the crude detail that Apollo made the Fates drunk with wine (mentioned with ⟦3⟧ by the scholiast on ⟦4⟧), one does not know. Euripides Alc. 12 ⟦5⟧; 33 ⟦6⟧. The story stood in Hesiod (schol. ⟦7⟧), certainly with this detail; but A. sometimes likes to bring out quite crude details of the story, e.g. ⟦8⟧
having tripped the Fates with a cunning trick
725 ⟦1⟧ as ⟦2⟧⟦3⟧ (when Zeus had given Apollo into servitude to Admetus because of the killing of the Cyclopes, which A. perhaps presupposes, perhaps cancels). 726
for being a holy man I happened upon a holy one

⟦1⟧: optative in the subordinate clause of a general statement, as ⟦2⟧ and often in Sophocles, ⟦3⟧ etc., Bruhn Appendix p. 78. On 728 cf. 172 ⟦4⟧. ⟦5⟧ occurs only here; very probable and very easy is Davies' conjecture ⟦6⟧, from ⟦7⟧ ⟦8⟧, ⟦9⟧ 488.
I wait to become a listener
⟦1⟧ only here, not yet decided, wavering to both sides, and thus as much as ⟦2⟧. Wecklein cites for the connection with only one infinitive, without disjunction, Homer Θ 167 ⟦3⟧, ⟦4⟧.
to turn the horses and fight face to face
